transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12 | Time: 4:00 PM PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jesse Patel (Redwood AE), Mariana Soto (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Zephyr - Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Zephyr - Platform Engineer), Samir Gupta (Zephyr - PM)

Summary (auto): Align on POC scope and integration plan; determine success metrics and benchmark plan; agree timeline and deliverables.

[00:00] Jesse: all right everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jesse from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we also have Mariana, our SE. can each of you do a quick intro?
[00:12] Laura: yeah hi i'm laura kim head of ml at zephyr analytics. we own the recommendation and summarization models.
[00:18] Ethan: ethan here, platform eng, i'll handle infra and security side.
[00:22] Samir: samir product, focused on integrations and timelines.
[00:26] Mariana: great, thanks. quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and then integration details around the SDK and open ai compatible endpoints, plus function calling and structured outputs.
[01:05] Jesse: to start, can you walk us through what a successful POC looks like from zephyr's perspective?
[01:12] Laura: sure. three things mainly: 1) latency targets — we want p95 response <350ms for short prompts (about 128 tokens) and <800ms for longer 512-token requests when possible; 2) quality — outputs must match our golden prompts at >=92% pass rate on our eval set; 3) operational — easy to integrate using our existing openai compatible clients and SSO/KMS for keys, and clear audit logs.
[01:40] Mariana: quick clarifying q, when you say "openai compatible" do you mean you expect identical REST endpoints and function-calling semantics?
[01:46] Laura: yes ideally. we have a bunch of SDK wrappers and serverless lambdas that call OpenAI endpoints, so minimal changes is ideal.
[01:54] Jesse: understood. on the latency side we typically recommend pinning a dedicated instance for a POC to hit consistent p95s — that also helps the throughput numbers.
[02:05] Ethan: what's the expected concurrency we should plan for? our prod traffic peaks at 60 rps across a few endpoints but the initial POC will be lower.
[02:14] Samir: for the POC we can target a synthetic load of 10-20 rps to simulate spikes, and baseline 5 rps steady state.
[02:21] Mariana: ok we'll size the benchmark for 5 rps baseline, 20 rps spike, with average prompt length of 180 tokens and max of 1k tokens for a few heavy calls.
[02:33] Jesse: good. for pass/fail let's propose: latency p95 under 400ms for 128 tokens, p95 under 900ms for 512 tokens, throughput goal sustaining 20 rps with 95% success, and quality >= 92% on your eval set. does that sound reasonable?
[02:52] Laura: that's reasonable but we might tighten latency if we see consistent overhead from routing. we also need cost estimates for both hosted vs dedicated.
[03:01] Jesse: we'll include unit cost estimates in the POC proposal.
[03:05] Ethan: security items: we need SOC2 docs, KMS integration for BYOK, SAML/SSO for console access, and audit logs with token-level detail.
[03:14] Mariana: we can share our security pack — SOC2, ISO evidence, architecture docs. for KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in private deployments and dedicated.
[03:27] Samir: timeline? how long do you usually run these POCs?
[03:31] Jesse: typical is 3-4 weeks. propose week 0 preparations (access + sample data), week 1 baseline benchmarks and infra setup, weeks 2-3 tuning/model selection + prompt iteration, week 4 acceptance and wrap-up.
[03:46] Laura: 4 weeks works. immediate blockers are credentials and a minimal sandbox to run benchmarks.
[03:53] Mariana: we'll need sample prompts and the expected JSON schema for structured output. do you have function calling usage today?
[03:59] Laura: yes — we use function-like calls to return structured entity lists and a few tooling hooks. examples: "extract_entities" returns a list of {name, type, confidence} and we do some multi-step tool calls to internal search.
[04:12] Jesse: ok, function calling compatibility is something Redwood supports through our OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK. mariana, can you explain the mapping?
[04:19] Mariana: we expose an endpoints that accept the openai flavor of messages + function definitions; we support synthesized call responses and structured JSON outputs. there may be small differences in field names but for the most part clients can reuse existing openai sdk calls with a different base_url and api_key.
[04:36] Ethan: what about streaming and partial responses for low latency UX?
[04:40] Mariana: streaming is supported; we also offer chunked streaming with event style frames similar to openai. there are some timing quirks with different runtimes but we can demo.
[04:48] Laura: also we have to preserve existing tool-calling orchestration — our orchestrator expects the exact function signature to be present.
[04:54] Mariana: noted. we'll validate function signature compatibility during the first benchmark run.
[05:01] Jesse: let's talk benchmarks. mariana will own the bench plan, but we need a reproducible harness. you mentioned sample traffic — ethan can you share a CSV of request patterns and sample prompts?
[05:12] Ethan: yes i can. it includes distribution of tokens, concurrency patterns, and a few edge-case prompts that we care about (multi-turn context).
[05:20] Mariana: ideal bench harness: run a 1 hour baseline at 5 rps, 30 minute spike at 20 rps, and a few long-tail tests with 1k token requests. capture p50, p95, p99 latency, error rate, and per-token cost. we'll also push your eval set through for quality scoring.
[05:40] Samir: how do we measure quality? we have an internal judge that checks for schema conformance plus a semantic similarity score.
[05:46] Mariana: we'll accept your judge scores — we run your evals inside the POC and produce a QC report. we recommend adding a few safety/ hallucination checks too.
[05:55] Laura: ok. two integration details: 1) our infra is in aws us-west-2 and we prefer inference to be in-region; 2) we need VPC peering or private endpoints — not public internet for the POC.
[06:08] Jesse: we can run the POC in our dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and enable VPC/private link for the duration. mariana — is there any leadtime?
[06:16] Mariana: provisioning dedicated nodes for a short POC can be done in days if the capacity is available; we'll confirm capacity in the proposal. if not available we can use our hosted sandbox with IP allowlist and private link as a fallback.
[06:29] Ethan: nice. about auth, we use SSO for console and API keys for service accounts, plus KMS-backed secrets for keys. can we do short-lived tokens?
[06:38] Jesse: yes, we support short-lived service tokens and SSO via SAML. we'll include examples in the integration guide.
[06:44] Laura: any gotchas with the openai sdk wrappers? some of our lambda functions rely on a particular field naming for function.call results.
[06:52] Mariana: we'll run a compatibility pass in week 1: call your lambdas against our endpoint in a dry run and capture diffs. small parsing changes are typically necessary but usually trivial.
[07:03] Samir: cost — can you give a rough delta between hosted and dedicated?
[07:09] Jesse: hosted is pay-as-you-go, typical higher per-token unit cost but no infra commitments. dedicated has a monthly reserved capacity with lower per-token and better latency. we'll include an example cost model in the proposal using your estimated token volumes.
[07:25] Laura: good. can you also include quantization/ model variant options? we might test a cheaper quantized variant for some endpoints.
[07:31] Mariana: absolutely, we'll include model/quantization matrix and recommended profiles per workload type.
[07:38] Ethan: how do logs and traces look? we need request->response tracing and token-level cost breakdowns exposed via console or API.
[07:46] Mariana: console has per-request traces, token breakdowns, and you can export logs to your SIEM. for private deployments we can push logs to your cloud logs too.
[07:55] Jesse: wrapping up, let's confirm the concrete next steps and owners.
[08:00] Samir: yes please.
[08:02] Jesse: action items we discussed earlier: mariana will draft the benchmark plan and metrics; i'll send the POC proposal and pricing; ethan will provide traffic profile and infra constraints; laura will share eval prompts and expected schema. target dates we put in the notes.
[08:18] Laura: we also need the security pack and SOC2 evidence.
[08:21] Mariana: i'll attach the security pack in the follow-up email.
[08:24] Jesse: cool. schedule wise let's tentatively block 2025-03-24 for kickoff once the proposal is accepted—that gives a week to exchange creds and samples.
[08:32] Samir: works for us.
[08:34] Ethan: one last q — will you provide an OpenAI-compat base_url and example curl and python sdk snippet?
[08:41] Mariana: yes we'll include sample curl/python/node snippets and a short migration guide.
[08:45] Laura: great, that's helpful.
[08:48] Jesse: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc pack and proposal.
[08:53] (overlap) Samir: thanks team.
